turns.text: Limbs heavy before the eyes agree to open — a leaden pull behind the ribs that isn't sleep and isn't quite waking either, some rented weight still draining out through a jack nobody remembers plugging in. The pod lid hasn't cracked. Doesn't want to. Whatever the body just finished renting out, it wants five more minutes it doesn't have.

the pod reads OCCUPANT: ACTIVE — SESSION COMPLETE across its fogged lid, sleep-zone rows stretching dim and coffin-shaped in either direction, each one leased down to the minute. a thin jingle threads in through the shared speaker line, the same six bars it always is, something about a tuna-flavored energy surge, looping under whatever's left of the dream before the billing cuts it off clean. overhead, a meter clicks upward by one more decimal, patient, unbothered by whether anyone inside is ready.

Paws find the seam of the lid before the rest of the body's caught up to being awake, pressing until it gives with a hiss of stale, recycled air. An electrode still clings behind one ear, tacky, unwilling to let go without a fight — teeth catch the wire and worry it loose, the taste of adhesive and old current bitter enough to finish waking what the jingle couldn't.

the electrode comes away with a soft pop, the readout above the pod flickering from ACTIVE to a running tally instead — a number that only ever climbs, red digits ticking off what tonight's rented dream cost against what's already owed. down the row, most of the pods stay dark and sealed, their occupants still mid-lease, unaware or past caring. a maintenance drone glides the aisle on its slow circuit, uninterested in anything that's already sitting up.

The tally gets one flat look and no more attention than the jingle got — old math, same shape every time, never worth the energy of minding closely. Paws find the aisle floor, cold through the pads, and ears swivel toward a sound bleeding in from some sector over — not the tally's quiet click but something louder, relentlessly bright, pitched like it's daring anyone nearby not to smile.

the corridor bends toward Pawsitivity Sector's shared feed wall, a bank of screens looping the same manic broadcast on every panel — a smile too wide to be anyone's own choosing, words stacking faster than they can be read, HAPPY bleeding into itself until half the letters give up holding their shape: H̶A̶P̵P̶Y̵H̸A̷P̴P̸Y̵. the volume's tuned for engagement metrics, not comfort, loud enough to rattle the grating underfoot two corridors off.

That volume gets no closer inspection — ears pin flat against it, whole body angling away before the decision to flee finishes forming. A service grate off the corridor's low side offers somewhere the sound can't follow at full strength, and the body takes it without checking twice, collar tag chirping one soft, unimpressed beep against the throat with every stride, marking the balance nobody asked it to keep.

   > ~ <        one bar left, keep moving

the shaft climbs cool and narrow through insulation gone soft with age, service ducts breathing warmer air down from somewhere above, colder air pulling up from somewhere below. faint through the metal: rain, real rain, the first honest sound in the whole complex, growing louder rung by rung toward a grate at the top left unlatched by whoever last used this route to leave.

That first taste of outside air hits before the grate even finishes swinging clear — cold, wet, unmetered, nothing about it billed to anyone. Lungs pull it in deep, twice, three times, the leaden pull from the pod finally thinning enough to let the legs move like they mean it.

the alley outside runs narrow between two service walls, rain coming down steady, gutters already running full. up on a fire escape two landings above, a compact shape sits hunched over a length of stripped cable, one ear cocked at an angle no ear grows into naturally, jaw working slow and patient at the insulation — testing it, tasting it, the way something looks for a way in rather than a way to eat. it doesn't glance down.

That ear-angle reads as somebody else's craft, not a threat — filed the same way a market's boundary marks get filed, a nod paid in stillness rather than approach. Doesn't linger under the fire escape. Cuts along the wall instead, rain flattening the fur down fast, glad of the cold after however many hours the pod's manufactured warmth stole.

the alley opens onto a lot flattened down to gravel and standing water, chain-link sagging at one corner where enough paws have pushed through it to keep the gap permanent. beyond it, rooftops step down toward the district's edge, puddles catching neon in long, broken smears across the gravel, one shallow pool near the fence deep enough to hold a full reflection if a body cared to look.

That pool gets a slow approach, thirst outweighing caution for once, nose dipping toward the surface before the tongue commits to anything. The reflection holds steady in the standing water, close enough to touch, ordinary.

the water holds the reflection the way water always does, until it doesn't — a half-second where the surface carries more than one shape looking back, layered thin as static over static, and something in it isn't blinking on the same rhythm anything alive blinks on. it doesn't say anything. it doesn't need to. then the wind crosses the pool, the layers scatter into ordinary ripples, and the reflection goes back to being just tired eyes and wet whiskers, nothing else.

The flinch happens before any reason for it arrives — a full-body flat-eared recoil off the pool's edge, paws skidding twice on wet gravel before catching. Doesn't drink. Doesn't look back at the water either. Whatever that was, it doesn't have a smell or a sound to catalogue it by, and nothing without either of those gets trusted long enough to investigate.

the lot stays exactly as ordinary as it was a moment before, gravel and rain and sagging fence, nothing in the pool now but sky and neon smear and the ordinary dark. two blocks off, Pawsitivity Sector's feed wall keeps looping its too-wide smile into the wet air, thinner out here, easier to ignore at this distance.

Distance does what the vent shaft couldn't, the broadcast fading down to something background-level, filed next to the tally and the jingle on the same shelf as everything else here that never actually stops. Finds a dry lip of concrete under the fence's overhang and settles there instead, the leaden pull from earlier creeping back in now that there's nothing left demanding a decision.

the overhang keeps most of the rain off, gravel dry in a shallow crescent worn smooth by however many nights of other bodies choosing the same spot. somewhere back in the complex, the meter over an empty pod is still climbing by its patient decimal, whether or not anything's occupying the lease to justify it — debt doesn't need a tenant to keep counting.

Eyes go to slits, the ache behind the ribs settling into something closer to ordinary tiredness now, the rented kind and the honest kind finally hard to tell apart. One ear stays angled back toward the fence gap out of habit, the rest already halfway toward whatever sleep doesn't get billed by the minute.

rain keeps finding the gravel outside the overhang's reach, the district's hum settling into its low late register, feed wall and meter and everything else built to keep running long after whoever's watching stops paying attention. nothing out here resolves the tally. it just gets quieter around it, same as every other debt this city's ever let go uncollected till morning.
